title: Shared fixture for spawning jit in CLI tests
description:
Give CLI integration tests one shared fixture that spawns `jit`, so no test file needs its own binary locator, repository setup, environment handling or id scraping.

## Background

No shared subprocess fixture exists. `fn jit_binary` is defined in 56 files under `crates/jit/tests/`; 43 files spawn through `assert_cmd`'s `cargo_bin!` and 69 through `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_jit")`. 56 files define a local `setup_test_repo` or `setup_repo`, and 33 more define differently named setups. 114 `split_whitespace` sites in 39 files parse human-readable output, most of them to scrape created ids. 20 test files and 8 source test modules hand-roll `git init`.

A few files remove chosen `JIT_*` variables (`steering_scenarios.rs`, `repo_discovery_tests.rs`, `profile_acceptance_tests.rs`, `project_config_tests.rs`, `failure_probe_fixture.rs`), but nothing removes them all. The product reads `JIT_AGENT_ID` at 10 sites, plus `JIT_DATA_DIR`, `JIT_WORKTREE_*`, `JIT_ALLOW_DELETION` and `JIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, so a developer's agent identity and data-directory overrides reach most spawned processes.

Shared test support (`crate::test_utils`, `crate::test_harness`, `crate::test_taxonomy`) is compiled once under `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))`, and every integration target enables that feature through the crate's self dev-dependency. `assert_cmd` is a dev-dependency, so library test support cannot name it. `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jit` is set only while an integration target compiles.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Shared test support provides one CLI process fixture. It owns a temporary repository, which is uninitialised, initialised by `jit init`, or a repository from shared test support handed to it, and it removes the repository on drop.
- [hard] REQ-02: The fixture locates the `jit` binary built for the calling integration target through one shared construction path, so a test names no binary path, `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jit` or `cargo_bin!`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every process the fixture spawns starts with no inherited `JIT_*` variable. A test sets one only through the fixture, and the setting reaches that process alone.
- [hard] REQ-04: On request the fixture initialises git in its repository, with a fixed author identity and no dependency on the developer's global git configuration. It does so through a shared test-support function that in-process tests can also call.
- [hard] REQ-05: The fixture reads the ids of issues it creates from `--json` output.
- [hard] REQ-06: The environment scrub, git initialisation and id reading each have one owning test, and each of those tests passes alone and in parallel with the rest.
- [hard] REQ-07: The fixture adds no integration target; it lives in the shared test-support surface.

## Notes

The fixture hands tests a `std::process::Command` or a thin wrapper around one, so tests keep `assert_cmd`'s assertion traits from their own dev-dependency. It adds no integration target (`@/inv/bounded-rust-build-footprint`). `dev/TESTING.md` names it as the way to spawn `jit`.

planning.outcome: One shared test-support fixture spawns jit over a temporary repository it owns, with inherited JIT_* variables removed.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One new test-support module with its own unit tests; no consumer is migrated here.

title: Tests read shared process environment only under the environment guard
description:
Close the remaining gap in process-state isolation: tests that read environment variables other tests set must hold the shared guard.

## Background

`EnvGuard` and `CurrentDirGuard` in `crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs` are the only mutators of the environment and working directory, enforced by `crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/process_state_policy_tests.rs`. Each serialises on a static mutex, recovers after poisoning and restores on drop; guards do not nest. Code that reads the environment without holding the guard is not serialised, so a test whose code under test reads `JIT_AGENT_ID`, `JIT_DATA_DIR` or another variable that a concurrent test sets under the guard can observe the other test's value. Known `EnvGuard` users are tests in `config.rs`, `serve.rs`, `crates/server/src/lib.rs`, `storage/json.rs`, `commands/hooks.rs` and `commands/claim.rs`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every test whose code under test reads a process environment variable that some test sets under `EnvGuard` holds `EnvGuard` for that read, or passes the value explicitly instead.
- [hard] REQ-02: No lock other than the two shared guards serialises environment or working-directory access in test code.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each affected test passes alone, in any order and in parallel with the rest.

planning.outcome: Each test that reads a variable another test sets holds the shared environment guard.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: An audit of a short list of guarded variables against their read sites.

footprint.uncertainty: The unguarded readers are found by auditing each EnvGuard-set variable against its read sites; candidates are the tests of config.rs, serve.rs, commands/claim.rs, commands/hooks.rs, storage/json.rs and crates/server/src/lib.rs.

title: Profiled-repository fixture lock waits are bounded
description:
Stop profiled-fixture consumers from timing out on the fixture's cross-process build lock or silently rebuilding a cold entry under it.

## Background

`profiled_repository_fixture` in `crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs` serves a nextest setup-script receipt when one exists and otherwise builds the entry directly under a cross-process lock.

On main at load 12, six consumers of the `jit-dogfood` profile time out at 20 s: the four `fast_rules cli_warnings_integration_tests` and the two `test_utils::tests::test_profiled_*` tests. Each calls `profiled_repository_fixture("jit-dogfood", …)`. With no nextest setup-script receipt for its test, the fixture falls back to a direct build under a cross-process lock. `.config/nextest.toml` names the setup-script consumers test by test, so these six get no receipt. They then either wait on the lock or each rebuild a cold key.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A consumer that finds no setup-script receipt takes the direct path deliberately and builds the entry at most once per key across the run. Concurrent consumers of the same key wait for that one build and then read the published entry, so no consumer rebuilds silently under the lock.
- [hard] REQ-02: A wait on the cross-process build lock is bounded below the per-test timeout. A wait that reaches the bound fails, naming the lock, the key and the holder, instead of running into the test runner's timeout.
- [hard] REQ-03: Tests observe both causes on a cold cache with no receipt environment. Several concurrent consumers of one profile finish within 5 s at load ≤ 10 and build the entry exactly once. A consumer facing a lock held past the bound fails with the named error.

planning.outcome: Profiled-fixture consumers make each entry once and never wait on the lock past the per-test bound.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One file family (`test_utils.rs`; 1 file) with one concern: the fixture's build lock and its once-per-key build.

title: Profiled-repository fixture keyed only on its inputs
description:
Key the profiled-repository fixture cache on what the fixture is built from, so test binaries share an entry and a rebuild without a source change costs nothing.

## Background

`profiled_repository_fixture` in `crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs` keys its cache (`profiled_repository_fixture_key`) on SHA-256 hashes of the setup executable (`current_exe`), an optional scenario executable and the captured package closure (`capture_profile_package_closure`: path, bytes and mode). Each test binary therefore gets its own key, and every rebuild invalidates every key. Cold keys after a rebuild cost 5.5-8 s of suite clock and push the profiled-fixture tests past the 20 s per-test bound under host load. Entries are never collected: `target/jit-profiled-repository-fixtures` held 1,341 entries (747 MB). No crate-source digest exists; `crates/jit/build.rs` emits only `JIT_BUILD_PROFILE` and `JIT_BUILD_TARGET`. Callers pass a scenario executable in `cli_item_validate/main.rs` and `cli_item_validate/derived_state_repair_tests.rs`, and `None` elsewhere. The fixture's cross-process build lock already bounds its waits below the per-test timeout and builds each key once.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The fixture key is a digest of the captured package closure, a digest of the `jit` crate's source and the fixture's setup-contract token, and includes no executable's bytes or path.
- [hard] REQ-02: Test binaries built from the same source share one entry per profile, and a rebuild without a source or package change reuses it.
- [hard] REQ-03: The fixture takes no scenario-executable argument, and no caller passes one.
- [hard] REQ-04: The cache keeps at most one entry per fixture profile: publishing a new entry removes that profile's older entries, without disturbing a concurrent reader of the current one.
- [hard] REQ-05: The fixture's own tests prove that the key is stable across executables and changes with a package or source byte.

planning.outcome: The profiled-repository fixture key derives from package bytes and crate source, and stale entries are collected.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: File family: the profiled-repository fixture and its six direct callers. Concern: the fixture's cache key; the callers change only by a compile-forced dropped argument.

title: Gate evaluation tests stop re-asserting projected exit codes

The exit-code projection suite (`cli_issue/command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs`) binds each command-to-exit-code row in both invocation forms, and its wildcard rows (`*` with 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 and 11) bind every command. Outside it, a subprocess test asserts success or failure and the property it adds, such as a JSON verdict, an error envelope code, remediation text or empty stdout. It names a numeric exit code only for a command and code pair the projection has no row for. The sweep counts numeric `.code(N)`, single- and multi-line `status.code()` comparisons with `Some(...)` (literal, `ExitCode::X` or derived), symbolic `ExitCode::X.code()`, and helpers that take an expected code.

Exit-code assertion sites in `crates/jit/tests/cli_gate`: `gate_evaluate_exit_code_test.rs` (13), `gate_evaluate_all_test.rs` (9), `gate_cli_integration_test.rs` (7), `gate_status_all_strict_test.rs` (5), `gate_evaluate_rerun_test.rs` (5), `gate_preset_apply_json_failure_test.rs` (2), `gate_findings_test.rs` (1), `bracket_coverage_gate_run_test.rs` (1), `gate_status_all_lean_response_test.rs` (1). `gate_evaluate_exit_code_test.rs` has 13 tests of gate evaluate exits 0, 4, 10, 3 and 2; its added property is the JSON verdict each run reports.

This entry covers `gate_evaluate_exit_code_test.rs`, `gate_evaluate_all_test.rs`, `gate_evaluate_rerun_test.rs`, `bracket_coverage_gate_run_test.rs`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No test in these files asserts a numeric exit code for a command and code pair the projection binds; each asserts success or failure instead.
